in_hebrew.name: לינדסי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word לינדה (lindah) which means 'fair, light, or gentle'. It is derived from the root לין (lin) which means 'flexible' or 'soft'. In the Bible, there is no character named Lindsy, but the name could potentially be derived from Linnea, a name found in the Old Testament (Song of Solomon 4:12-15).

in_greek.name: Λίνδσυ
in_greek.long_meaning: There is no direct Greek equivalent to the name Lindsy. However, it could potentially be derived from the Greek name Λυδια (Lydia), which means 'from Lydia' or 'member of the Lydian people'. Lydia was a prominent early Christian convert in the New Testament (Acts 16:14-15).
